bottom_line: The AI stock boom is cracking. The S&P 500 and Dow are now in a correction (a big drop from their recent highs), and the Fed (the people who set interest rates) is talking about raising rates to fight inflation, not cutting them to help stocks.

stories.title: AI stocks get crushed
stories.real: Anthropic sold shares to the public at $83 each and raised $93.5 billion in a record IPO, then its stock fell on day two. That dragged down the whole tech sector. The Nasdaq wiped out its 2026 gain, and Nvidia is on its longest weekly losing streak since 2008.

stories.title: Fed leans toward raising rates
stories.real: Inflation is still too high, so Fed officials like Lisa Cook and Paulson are saying rate hikes are needed. Some are even discussing a bigger-than-usual hike at the Dec. 9 meeting. They mostly agree on hiking and disagree on how fast.
stories.you: Higher rates usually make credit cards, car loans and mortgages more expensive, and the Fed is not coming to rescue falling stock prices.

stories.title: Gold takes a big fall
stories.real: Gold dropped nearly 9% this week, its worst week since March, and hit a 14-month low. Traders expecting higher rates pulled money out, and the AI sell-off added to the selling.
stories.you: Gold was not a safe place to hide this week, so anyone who bought it for safety took a loss too.

stories.title: Trump threatens overseas data centers
stories.real: Trump said he wants to stop U.S. companies from building AI data centers in other countries and threatened a 'tremendous tax.' He gave few details, and people on his own team said they were hearing about it for the first time.
stories.you: Unclear rules like this make AI companies harder to value, and that adds to the pressure on tech stocks people own through funds.

stories.title: Jobs are holding up
stories.real: The number of people asking for unemployment help went up a little, but it is still low compared to history. The job market is still strong even while stocks fall.
stories.you: Most people's paychecks are not in danger right now, even though their investment accounts are taking a hit.
